title: Private Deployments: Comprehensive Deployment & Day-2 Operations Guide
author: Ava Chen
content:
Summary:

This document is a single-source deployment and day-2 operations guide for Redwood Inference private deployments (VPC, customer-managed cloud, and on-prem). It consolidates recommended reference architectures, packaging instructions, customer requirements, day-2 operations checklists, and safe upgrade/rollback procedures. Intended audience: solutions engineers, SREs, and customer ops teams supporting private deployment engagements.

Goals and scope:
- Provide repeatable, secure deployment patterns for VPC and on-prem customers.
- Define customer requirements and prechecks to accelerate onboarding.
- Document packaging and install options for air-gapped and internet-connected environments.
- Describe operational runbooks for day-2 activities, monitoring, backups, and incident response.
- Provide a conservative upgrade and rollback playbook with gating criteria and automation snippets.

Ownership and contacts:
- Owner: eng-private-deployments team (primary contact: Ava Chen, Solutions Engineering).
- Escalation: SRE on-call (pager), Platform Engineering (for kernel/runtime issues), Security (for incident review).

Reference architectures (high level):

1) VPC-hosted private control plane + customer-managed data plane (recommended for cloud-savvy customers)
- Description: Redwood control plane (managed) connects via secure peering/PrivateLink to customer VPC where inference runtime runs.
- Components: private control plane endpoint, customer VPC (subnets: control, compute, management), autoscaling GPU node pools, NAT gateway for selective outbound, S3-compatible object store for model artifact sync, KMS integration.
- Network requirements and CIDR examples:
  - Control plane CIDR: 10.240.0.0/16 (example)
  - Customer VPC compute subnets: 10.0.32.0/24 (gpu-pool-1), 10.0.33.0/24 (gpu-pool-2)
  - Minimum outbound allowed: control plane endpoint, KMS endpoint, package mirror, metrics sink
- Security considerations: PrivateLink/Peering, mTLS for RPC, RBAC enforced via control plane tokens, customer KMS for secrets.

2) Fully private VPC (preferred for regulated workloads)
- Description: Both control plane and data plane are deployed inside customer account/VPC; Redwood provides an appliance-style control plane bundle.
- Components: internal control plane, HA PostgreSQL or managed RDS, object store (S3 or on-prem equivalent), GPU node pools, bastion for admin access.
- High-level HA topology: 3 control-plane replicas in separate AZs, at least 2 postgresql replicas + replicas for object store, cross-AZ load balancer.

3) On-prem / Air-gapped reference architecture
- Description: All components run in customer on-prem datacenter with no direct internet access. Packaging includes offline artifacts and installation appliance.
- Components: air-gapped package bundle, local artifact registry (Harbor), local model store, internal metrics/alerting stack, optional HSM/KMS integration.

Pre-deployment customer requirements (checklist):
- Administrative:
  1) Designated customer technical lead and SRE contacts (name, email, pager).
  2) Maintenance window cadences and change freeze windows.
  3) Support access: bastion host or direct VPN/Direct Connect.
- Networking:
  1) VPC CIDR allocations and subnet mapping (compute, management, control).
  2) Required egress to Redwood control endpoints (or private connectivity).
  3) Firewall rules for internal services (ports table below).
- Compute & Storage:
  1) GPU types and counts by capacity plan (NVIDIA A10G / A100 / H100 etc.).
  2) Node sizing: CPU/memory per node, disk sizing for model cache (recommend 1–8TB NVMe depending on workload).
  3) Object store access (S3-compatible endpoint) and IAM role/policy prepared.
- Security & Compliance:
  1) KMS/HSM availability and access model.
  2) Audit logging sink (SIEM) and retention policy.
  3) RBAC groups and initial admin users.

Required ports and services (table):
- Control plane -> Data plane: 443 (mTLS control RPC), 8000 (metrics ingest, if configured)
- Data plane -> Control plane: ephemeral TLS ports for agent communication (443), SSH for troubleshooting (restricted)
- Model fetch: 443 (S3-compatible API) or internal artifact registry ports (5000/5443)
- Inter-node communication: 2379/2380 (etcd) if using in-cluster state store, overlay networking (VXLAN) ports as per CNI

On-prem packaging & installation options:

Packaging formats provided:
- Installer bundle (tar.gz) with signed artifacts and an install script for online installs.
- Air-gapped bundle: signed images (OCI layout), Helm charts, RPM/DEB packages, and artifact transfer manifest.
- Appliance image: OVA/ISO for hypervisor-based installs (for customers preferring a single VM bundle).

Installation patterns (high level):
1) Cloud-managed VPC (fast path):
  - Pre-checks performed by solutions engineer.
  - Customer provides IAM role, subnets, and KMS key.
  - Run bootstrap script to deploy control-plane connectors and runtime node pools via Terraform modules provided.
2) Customer-managed control & data plane (self-hosted in account):
  - Provide CloudFormation/Terraform templates and state examples.
  - CI/CD pipeline recommended for applying control-plane changes.
3) Air-gapped / on-prem:
  - Transfer signed bundle to customer registry.
  - Install base OS packages, apply kernel tuning (see table below), install container runtime, import images, and install via Helm with offline values.yaml.

Kernel and runtime tuning recommendations (table):
- File descriptors: 100k+ per host
- vm.swappiness: 1
- net.core.rmem_max / wmem_max: 16MB
- nvidia persistence mode: enabled
- HugePages: enabled for high-throughput workloads (configurable)

Day-2 operations (runbooks and checklists):

Daily checks (SRE checklist):
- Verify cluster health: control plane pods, etcd status, node readiness.
- Check model sync jobs: recent sync success timestamp.
- Monitor GPU utilization, memory pressure, and KV cache hit rates.
- Alert review: unresolved P1s, pager incidents.

Weekly and Monthly tasks:
- Rotate short-lived tokens and verify KMS key rotation has succeeded.
- Run performance smoke tests against representative prompts (automated harness).
- Validate backups and perform restore drill in staging.

Operational playbooks (selected):
1) Model sync failure
  - Symptoms: models unavailable, 404s from runtime, or stale models served.
  - Immediate steps: check object store connectivity, verify sync job logs, re-trigger sync with dry-run flag.
  - Recovery: re-sync specific model artifacts, restart model-manager pod, clear local cache for the model if corrupted.
2) Node GPU OOM or driver crash
  - Symptoms: node kernel OOM, processes restarted, GPU unavailable.
  - Immediate steps: cordon node, drain gracefully, capture dmesg and nvidia-smi logs, escalate to infra for replacement.
  - Recovery: reprovision node, restore model cache from warm cache snapshot, resume normal scheduling.
3) Control plane degraded (etcd/DB replication lag)
  - Symptoms: leader elections, control plane errors, elevated request latencies.
  - Immediate steps: check etcd member health, disk I/O, network partitions.
  - Recovery: add more IO, promote healthy replicas, or if necessary, failover using documented etcd restore playbook.

Monitoring, SLOs, and KPIs to instrument:
- API latency (p50/p95/p99) for generation endpoints: targets vary by deployment tier (example: p95 < 400ms for low-latency tier).
- Token throughput and per-token cost (billing metric).
- Model cache hit rate (goal > 90% for large-model workloads).
- GPU availability (target 99.9% uptime for dedicated clusters).
- Alert burn rate and Mean Time To Acknowledge (MTTA) targets.

Backups and disaster recovery:
- Database: nightly logical backups + WAL shipping for point-in-time recovery.
- Model artifacts: versioned object store snapshots with lifecycle policies.
- Restore drills: quarterly restore test to staging with documented time-to-restore targets.

Upgrade and rollback procedures (safe path):

Principles:
- All upgrades are staged: dev -> staging -> canary -> production.
- Keep rollback artifacts available and test rollback frequently.
- Gate upgrades on smoke tests and performance benchmarks.

Pre-upgrade checklist:
1) Confirm maintenance window and notify stakeholders.
2) Validate current backup health (DB and model artifacts).
3) Record current deployment manifests and image digests.
4) Run canary workload smoke tests and capture baseline metrics.

Upgrade steps (high level):
1) Build and publish signed artifacts to registry (CI step).
2) Apply upgrade to staging and run full integration tests (automated).
3) Deploy to canary subset (e.g., 10% of nodes or a single AZ) and validate:
   - Model serving correctness (output regression tests).
   - Latency and throughput vs baseline.
   - Resource usage (GPU/CPU/memory).
4) If canary succeeds, rollout in waves (by AZ/node-pool). Observe for 30–60 minutes between waves.

Rollback steps (if canary or wave fails):
1) Immediately stop further rollouts.
2) Re-deploy previous image digest and manifests to affected nodes using the recorded digests.
3) Verify failed conditions are resolved (smoke tests, metrics).
4) Open an incident review if root cause is unclear.

Automated rollback guardrails:
- Use rollout controllers that support automatic pause on metric regressions (e.g., Flux/Argo rollouts with metric analysis).
- Keep a pre-populated rollback playbook that references saved image digests and Helm values.

Post-upgrade validation and sign-off:
- Run regression suite (prompt-level checks) and compare quality metrics to baseline.
- Validate telemetry and billing pipelines are intact.
- Sign-off: Platform owner records results and updates release notes.

Security, compliance, and audit considerations:
- All installation artifacts are signed and checksummed.
- TLS and mutual auth enforced on control RPCs.
- Integration with customer KMS for secret management.
- Audit logging for admin operations retained per customer policy.

Appendices:
A. Example offline values.yaml snippet for Helm (air-gapped):
```
# values.yaml (snippet)
imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
registry: my-local-registry.internal:5443
images:
  runtime: my-local-registry.internal:5443/redwood/runtime@sha256:abcdef...
  model-manager: my-local-registry.internal:5443/redwood/model-manager@sha256:12345...
objectStore:
  endpoint: https://my-internal-s3.local
  bucket: redwood-models
  region: local
```

B. Kernel tuning commands (example):
- sysctl -w vm.swappiness=1
- sysctl -w fs.file-max=200000
- echo 1 > /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled

C. Quick rollback command example (helm):
- helm rollback redwood-runtime 3 --namespace redwood
- kubectl set image deployment/redwood-runtime redwood-runtime=my-local-registry/internal/redwood/runtime@sha256:previousDigest

D. Customer requirements table (sample entries):
- Name: PaymentVault Inc. | Deployment type: Air-gapped on-prem | GPU: 4x A100 | KMS: Thales HSM | Compliance notes: SOC2, PCI scoping required
- Name: FinApps Ltd. | Deployment type: VPC private control plane | GPU: mixed A10G + A100 | KMS: AWS KMS CMK | Connectivity: PrivateLink required
